blocks.text: AZARIAH SON OF ODED, ON WHOM “THE SPIRIT OF GOD CAME” · TWO KINGDOMS
Azariah. One speech to King Asa, and a reform that followed it.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
Two kingdoms 930–586 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Asa
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
“The Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded: and he went out to meet Asa”.
THE CALL
How the word came
“The Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded: and he went out to meet Asa”. 2 Chronicles 15:1–2
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before Asa
KING OF JUDAH
Asa
“The LORD is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.”
2 Chronicles 15:2 (KJV) →
THE MESSAGE
The word in its main themes
Seek him and he will be found
“if ye seek him, he will be found of you”
2 Chronicles 15:2 (KJV) →
A people without the true God
“Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.”
2 Chronicles 15:3 (KJV) →
Be strong
“Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.”
2 Chronicles 15:7 (KJV) →
THE WORD TO …
To whom the word was spoken
TO ASA, AND ALL JUDAH AND BENJAMIN
“Hear ye me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin; The LORD is with you, while ye be with him”
2 Chronicles 15:2 (KJV) →
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Oded, his father
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textScripture names Azariah only in this chapter and does not tell of his death. 2 Chronicles 15:1
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
The days of the judges
Matthew Poole (1683–1685); John Gill (1748–1763); Joseph Benson (1811–1818); C. Vitringa, as reported by Keil
Poole: “Generally of the whole nation of Israel in former times, and especially in the times of the judges”; Gill agrees that it refers to “time past”. 2 Chronicles 15:3–6 [81][33][3][59]
Judah's own recent years
Geneva notes (1599); the Syriac and Arabic versions and Rashi, as reported by Keil
The Geneva note: “For the space of twelve years under Rehoboam, and three years under Abijah, religion was neglected”. 2 Chronicles 15:3 [22][59]
The northern kingdom at that time
The Targum, Tremellius and Grotius, as reported by Keil
Keil reports this view and calls it “decidedly erroneous”, since no such disorder is told of the northern kingdom's first thirty years. 2 Chronicles 15:3 [59]
No fixed time: truths for every age
C. F. Keil (1872)
The verse “contains no verb”; the prophet was “giving utterance to truths which have force at all times”, known in the days of the judges and to be known more deeply later. 2 Chronicles 15:3 [59]
The Chronicler's own reflection
W. E. Barnes (1899)
Verses 3–6 “contain the reflections of the Chronicler himself on the whole previous course of Israelite history”; Azariah's exhortation continues in verse 7. 2 Chronicles 15:3–7 [108]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 1
2 Chronicles 15
PASSAGES · 1
2 Chronicles 15:1–15
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Kings does not mention Azariah; his speech is in Chronicles only.
Chronicles does not say where Azariah met Asa, only that he “went out to meet Asa” as the king returned from the war with Zerah.
Verse 8 speaks of “the prophecy of Oded the prophet”; who is meant is a question on Oded's page.
